questions.stem: Consider the following about HYDROCARBONS. 1. Alkanes are saturated and have the general formula CnH2n+2. 2. Alkenes contain at least one C=C double bond and exhibit geometric (cis-trans) isomerism. 3. Benzene is an aromatic hydrocarbon with the formula C6H6 and each C-C bond length is intermediate between a single and double bond. 4. Methane is the principal component of LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas). Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — LPG is mainly PROPANE (C3H8) and BUTANE (C4H10), not methane. Methane is the main component of CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) and of BIOGAS. Statements 1, 2, 3 are standard organic-chemistry facts.

questions.stem: Match the polymer with its monomer. A. Polythene. B. PVC. C. Teflon. D. Nylon-6,6. List-II: 1. Tetrafluoroethene. 2. Ethene. 3. Vinyl chloride. 4. Hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid.
questions.explanation: Polythene (polyethylene) — monomer ethene (CH2=CH2). PVC (polyvinyl chloride) — vinyl chloride (CH2=CHCl). Teflon (PTFE) — tetrafluoroethene (CF2=CF2). Nylon-6,6 — condensation of hexamethylenediamine (H2N-(CH2)6-NH2) + adipic acid (HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH).

questions.stem: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Formaldehyde (HCHO) — used in preservation of biological specimens
Acetic acid (CH3COOH) — used as a disinfectant and bleach

questions.explanation: Acetic acid is vinegar (~5-8 % aqueous) — a mild food acid used in cooking and pickling, NOT as a primary disinfectant or bleach. Disinfectants are chlorine, phenol, Dettol (chloroxylenol). Bleach is sodium hypochlorite. Other three pairings are correct (ethanol in drinks, methanol poisonous, formaldehyde in formalin used for preserving specimens in biology labs).

questions.stem: The 'greenhouse potential' of methane (CH4) over a 100-year period is ROUGHLY how many times that of CO2?
questions.explanation: GWP (100-year) of CH4 is ~28 per IPCC AR5 (higher on 20-year scale, ~84-87). Nitrous oxide N2O is ~265. SF6 is ~23,500. Cached numbers that recur in UPSC/GK/Envt questions.

questions.stem: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is produced by reacting salicylic acid with:
questions.explanation: Aspirin is an ester of the phenolic -OH of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O. Salicylic acid + (CH3CO)2O → acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) + CH3COOH. First synthesised by Bayer (Felix Hoffmann, 1897) as a safer alternative to salicylic acid itself, which was harsh on the stomach.

questions.stem: Consider the following about SOAPS and DETERGENTS. 1. Soaps are sodium/potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids. 2. Soaps do NOT work well in hard water because they form insoluble precipitates (scum) with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ ions. 3. Detergents work in hard water because their sulfonate head does not precipitate with Ca/Mg. 4. Both soaps and detergents clean by having a hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic tail that solubilises oil/grease in water via micelles. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Soap: R-COONa. Scum = Ca(RCOO)2. Detergent: R-SO3Na — the calcium sulfonate salt is soluble, so no scum. Cleaning mechanism identical — dual-character molecule forms micelles around grease droplets.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Molecular N2 does NOT absorb infrared radiation (its vibrational modes are IR-inactive because it is a homo-nuclear diatomic with no dipole moment). It is ~78 % of the atmosphere but not a greenhouse gas. CH4, N2O, O3, CO2, H2O, CFCs, HFCs, SF6 all ARE greenhouse gases.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the CORRECT IUPAC name of CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3?
questions.explanation: 4-carbon chain → 'butan-'. -OH is on C2 (numbering from the end that gives lowest locant to -OH). So butan-2-ol. 'Butan-3-ol' is the same molecule mis-numbered (numbering should always give the principal group the lowest locant — 2 not 3).
